title: Network & configuration check
intro: Checks your public address, NAT, clock, ports 80/443, DDNS resolution, certificate validity, certificate coverage of HTTPS sites, frp proxy conflicts and Intrusion Prevention's firewall sync. It queries the public IP lookup services configured for DDNS.

r.publicIPv4Fail: Could not determine the public IPv4 address
r.direct: This machine holds the public address {ip} directly
r.behindNat: Behind NAT: this machine only has a private address
r.cgnat: A carrier-grade NAT address ({ip}) was found on a network interface
r.clockUnknown: Could not measure the clock offset
r.port80Denied: No permission to listen on port 80
r.port443Denied: No permission to listen on port 443
r.direct6: This machine holds the public IPv6 address {ip} directly
r.webCertOk: All {count} HTTPS sites have a matching certificate
r.webCertMissing: Site {site} (port {port}) has no matching certificate for: {domains}
r.frpOk: No conflicts found for {count} frpc proxies
r.frpDuplicate: Several enabled frpc proxies are named {proxy}; only the first one takes effect
r.guardOk: Intrusion Prevention is synced to the system firewall with {bans} addresses banned
r.guardOS: This system has no nftables, so Intrusion Prevention only protects Gately's own services
r.guardUnsupported: The system kernel does not support nftables; Intrusion Prevention only applies to Gately's own services
r.guardMissing: Intrusion Prevention: the nft command was not found, so bans are not synced to the system firewall
r.guardPermission: Intrusion Prevention: no permission to change the firewall
r.guardError: Intrusion Prevention failed to write firewall rules: {error}
r.guardTrapSkipped: Trap ports {ports} are in use and were excluded
r.guardTrapUserspace: Firewall sync is not active, so Gately listens on the trap ports itself and only catches scans that complete the handshake
r.guardScanUnavailable: Port-scan detection is on but firewall sync is not active, so detection is not running
r.guardJailError: Intrusion Prevention jail {jail} has an error: {error}

h.publicIPv4Fail: Check outbound connectivity and DNS, or change the IP lookup URLs in the DDNS settings.
h.behindNat: Inbound access needs port forwarding on the router, UPnP, STUN, IPv6 or a tunnel (Tailscale, NetBird, frp, Cloudflare Tunnel).
h.cgnat: Your ISP may not give you a public IPv4 address. Use IPv6, STUN or a tunnel. Note that Tailscale also uses the 100.64.0.0/10 range.
h.clockSkew: A wrong clock breaks two-step verification codes and certificate validation. Enable NTP time sync.
h.portInUse: Normal if a Web Service listener of Gately uses it. Otherwise find the other program with ss -ltnp.
h.portDenied: Run as root, grant CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE, or listen on a higher port and forward to it.
h.ddnsMismatch: DNS caches may take a few minutes to refresh. If it persists, check the DDNS task log.
h.ddnsUnresolved: Create the record at your DNS provider or check the DDNS task log.
h.ddnsLookupFailed: Neither the local DNS nor public DNS answered, so it is unknown whether the record exists. Run the check again later; if it persists, check this host's DNS settings and outbound network.
h.certExpiring: Check the certificate renewal log; make sure DNS credentials or port 80 are reachable.
h.certExpired: Renew the certificate now from the SSL page and check the renewal log.
h.direct6: Services on this machine are reachable over IPv6 without port forwarding, as long as the router and local firewall allow the ports.
h.webCertMissing: Requests to these domains fail during the TLS handshake. Add a certificate that covers them on the Certificates page (a wildcard covers one subdomain level), or remove the domains from the site.
h.frpDuplicate: frp requires unique proxy names; rename the duplicates.
h.frpConflict: The frps server already has a proxy with this name, or the domain or remote port is taken. This usually happens when several devices share a copy of the same frpc config. Give each device's frpc a different user, or change the proxy names, domains and remote ports; sites behind a conflicting proxy time out.
h.guardMissing: Install nftables. For Docker, update to the latest image.
h.guardPermission: Writing to nftables requires root or CAP_NET_ADMIN. For Docker, add cap_add: [NET_ADMIN] to the compose file and use host networking.
h.guardUnsupported: The kernel does not have nf_tables enabled (Synology DSM, for example), and installing packages cannot fix that. Turn off "Sync to system firewall" in the Intrusion Prevention settings.
h.guardError: The kernel may be missing nftables modules, or nft is too old (0.9.0 or later is required).
h.guardTrapSkipped: Services listen on these ports, so trapping them would ban legitimate visitors. They were skipped.
h.guardScanUnavailable: See the Intrusion Prevention page for the firewall status and how to fix it.
h.guardJailError: Check the log file path, service unit or container name. When Gately runs in a container, mount the log directory into it.
